hbm-mrcd.name: Multiplexed Registered Clock Driver (MRCD)
hbm-mrcd.desc: Core logic device for high-bandwidth server memory modules, paired with the Multiplexed Data Buffer (MDB). It time-multiplexes data across two DRAM arrays without raising DRAM speed, doubling bandwidth. First generation: 8800 MT/s.

hbm-mdb.name: Multiplexed Data Buffer (MDB)
hbm-mdb.desc: Data buffer paired with the MRCD; it caches and multiplexes data streams from multiple DRAM ranks and outputs them to the CPU in time-division fashion, raising bandwidth without higher per-DRAM speed. First generation: 8800 MT/s.

hbm-rcd.name: Registered Clock Driver (RCD)
hbm-rcd.desc: Registered clock driver for server memory modules; it buffers and re-drives address, command and clock signals, improving signal integrity and supporting higher-capacity, higher-frequency modules. Up to 7200 MT/s, 4th sub-generation.

hbm-db.name: Data Buffer (DB)
hbm-db.desc: Data buffer paired with the RCD; it caches and re-drives data signals between the memory controller and DRAM, improving signal integrity and supporting larger-capacity, higher-frequency server memory modules. Mainly used in LRDIMM.

hbm-ckd.name: Client Clock Driver (CKD)
hbm-ckd.desc: Clock driver for client DDR5 memory modules; it buffers and re-drives the CPU-to-DRAM clock. From 6400 MT/s up, desktop and notebook modules need it for high-speed clock integrity and reliability. Meets JEDEC DDR5 CKD01, up to 7200 MT/s.

specs.v: I²C / I3C, dual side-band bus address access

hbm-pmic.name: Memory Module Power Management IC (PMIC)
hbm-pmic.desc: On-board power management IC for DDR5 server and client memory modules, providing regulated power and power management and working together with the memory interface and companion chips.

hbm-spd.name: Serial Presence Detect Hub (SPD Hub)
hbm-spd.desc: Serial presence detect hub for DDR5 memory modules; it stores module information (SPD) and manages the bus, forming the module companion chipset together with the memory interface chip.

hbm-ts.name: Memory Module Temperature Sensor (TS)
hbm-ts.desc: On-board temperature sensor for memory modules; it reports module temperature per JEDEC specifications and supports thermal management and throttling protection, used with the memory interface chip.

hbm-cxl-mxc.name: CXL Memory eXpander Controller (MXC)
hbm-cxl-mxc.desc: CXL Type 3 compliant memory expander controller; high-bandwidth, low-latency interconnect for CPUs and CXL devices, with cross-host memory pooling and sharing. Fits add-in cards (AIC), backplanes or EDSFF modules for TB-level expansion.

specs.v: Add-in card (AIC) / backplane / EDSFF memory module

hbm-pcie-retimer.name: PCIe Retimer (Gen5 / Gen6)
hbm-pcie-retimer.desc: Signal repeater for AI servers and cloud data centers: re-times, equalizes and adapts PCIe signals to improve signal integrity and reach. Supports PCIe 6.x / CXL 3.x (64 GT/s), PCIe 5.0 / CXL 2.0 (32 GT/s) and Gen3–Gen6 auto-negotiation.

rail-72.name: Server Slide Rail (7.2 mm)
rail-72.desc: Steel ball-bearing slide rail for rack-mounted equipment, inner/outer rail structure, 7.2 mm rail height; mounting holes in the rail body fit cabinet uprights, suited to chassis with tight height clearance.

specs.v: Cabinet uprights / chassis side walls (mounting holes)

rail-77.name: Server Slide Rail (7.7 mm)
rail-77.desc: Steel slide rail for rack-mounted equipment, 7.7 mm rail height, with mounting holes in the rail body; works with cabinet uprights for slide-out installation of the chassis.

rail-96.name: Server Slide Rail (9.6 mm)
rail-96.desc: Steel slide rail for rack-mounted equipment, inner/outer rail structure and 9.6 mm rail height, with mounting holes for slide-out and fixing of the chassis inside cabinets.

rail-128.name: Server Slide Rail (12.8 mm)
rail-128.desc: Steel ball-bearing slide rail for rack-mounted equipment, 12.8 mm rail height, with mounting holes at the ends and on the rail body for slide-out installation of the chassis inside cabinets.

rail-friction.name: Friction Slide Rail
rail-friction.desc: Friction slide rail without ball bearings; sliding comes from friction between rail body and slider. Simple structure with few parts, suited to light-load fixing and service access.

cable-arm.name: Server Cable Management Arm
cable-arm.desc: Cable management arm fitted at the rear of the slide rails; it secures and routes the cables at the server rear and extends with the server as it slides, preventing interference, pulling and wear during maintenance.

specs.v: Route cables at the server rear
